object_description: flat horizontal block-edge volume enclosing a central schoolyard
design_condition: The perimeter-enclosing volume is fitted to surrounding height differences and creates four use-specific outdoor spaces, including an introverted central schoolyard that is weakly connected to the neighborhood.

positive.statement: The flat, horizontally structured block-edge building is precisely fitted into the existing context by incorporating the surrounding height differences.
The central schoolyard is the identity-creating center of the school complex and is accessed from various sides via spacious staircases.
The internal organization is coherent and credibly implements the school's ‘under one roof’ principle.
The basic level is generously designed as an autonomous unit with flexible spaces, clear storage and short routes to the outdoor area.
The ring-shaped primary-level access provides visual contact and great flexibility of use.
The shallow building depth allows good daylight quality in all rooms.
The hybrid construction has a positive effect on primary energy and greenhouse-gas emissions.

negative.statement: It is questionable whether the courtyard can withstand the pressure of actual use and installations.
The introverted schoolyard is isolated from the neighborhood, barely visible and not very connected.
The urban integration of the existing gymnasium is also called into question.
The desired elegance is not achieved equally on all facades, where vertical openings compete with the pronounced horizontality.
The day-school access corridors appear too narrow, and the two music rooms have unfavorable proportions.
The large surface area of the building shell and extensive terrain movements have a negative impact on operational and gray energy.
The project has increased construction costs, particularly because of comparatively high land consumption.
